title: Cyrus and the Orbit
premise: Lena Nystrom, a terraformer and veteran cargo pilot, recognizes the crew of the returned ship Meridian as people she once knew—now decades younger, their memories intact but the massacre they fled erased from every official record. When the corporate authority that rewrote history begins hunting the de-aged survivors to finish the job, Lena must smuggle them to a rogue archive station while confronting her own complicity in staying silent twenty years ago. In the end, she broadcasts the true record to every colony at once, sacrificing her ship and her anonymity, and chooses to stay with the survivors in the orbit she can no longer pretend is neutral.
about_author: Silas Reyes is a former maritime logistics analyst who spent a decade writing about supply chains before turning to fiction about the people those chains forget. He lives near a decommissioned launch site and writes at night, when the satellites are easiest to see.

chapters.title: The Garden for Unborn Hands
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She tends the terraforming greenhouse on Ceres Station, reflecting on twenty years of hauling cargo through contested orbits and keeping her head down. A distress ping from deep space interrupts her routine. The emotional beat is quiet unease—the sense that invisibility is a debt that comes due.

chapters.title: Meridian, Returning
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The ship Meridian docks, its crew impossibly young—faces she knew as middle-aged now decades backward, memories intact. Among them is Tomas Reyes, who testified against the Halcyon Combine before vanishing. The beat is vertigo: recognition colliding with impossibility.

chapters.title: What Every Record Denies
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. He recounts the Kestrel Ring massacre—three hundred miners killed when they struck—and how the Combine erased it, then apparently reversed the survivors' aging to discredit them. Lena checks archives; nothing exists. The beat is horror at how thoroughly truth can be unwritten.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Looking Away
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, interwoven with flashbacks. She remembers the night of the massacre, docked nearby, choosing not to look, not to log what her sensors recorded. Guilt surfaces: she may still hold the raw data on an old drive. The beat is shame sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Combine's Long Arm
chapters.summary: POV of Ilsa Voss, Combine security director. Voss learns the Meridian survived and orders the de-aged crew declared unstable fabricators, warranting 'protective detention.' The reader sees the machinery of erasure from inside. The beat is cold, bureaucratic menace.

chapters.title: Contraband Passengers
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She hides the survivors aboard her freighter among legitimate cargo, using old smuggling routes to slip Combine checkpoints. Tomas insists on retrieving her sensor drive; she resists reliving that night. The beat is tense intimacy forged under threat.

chapters.title: The Archive That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. They reach Perihelion, a rogue station run by ex-archivists preserving forbidden records. There, Lena's drive confirms the massacre—and reveals Voss personally signed the order. But the Combine has traced them. The beat is vindication shadowed by encroaching danger.

chapters.title: Siege of Perihelion
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Combine forces blockade the station, demanding the 'delusional' passengers. The archivists offer asylum but no way out. Lena proposes broadcasting the record through the colony relay network instead of hiding it. The beat is defiance crystallizing into a plan.

chapters.title: Every Frequency at Once
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, climax. She flies her freighter straight into the relay hub, using her ship's transmitter to flood every colony channel with the massacre footage and Voss's order. Voss tries to jam and destroy her; the ship burns. The broadcast lands. The beat is sacrifice and triumph entangled.

chapters.title: The Orbit We Keep
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, resolution. Stranded but alive, she returns to Ceres with Tomas and the survivors. Investigations begin; Voss is arrested, though justice feels partial after three hundred names. Lena plants new seedlings in the garden—for people born into a truer world. The beat is hard-won, imperfect peace.
